desc: Run the existing brute-force BFS (N≤2000 path) on many small random graphs and record (features, dist(S,T), exact answer) to identify the formula pattern and exact impossibility condition (conjecture: graph is a path).
Derive and prove the correct formula from the data (partially done: path→−1 and same-biconnected→shortest-cycle hypotheses formed; Case-3 formula still unproven).

Build a brute-force verification harness (scratch script) running exact pair-BFS on exhaustive small graphs (N≤6) and parameterized families (path+branch at distance k, cycles with trees attached, two cycles joined by path, even/odd cycles) to pin down Case-3 formula, C4-adjacent answer, and parity effects.

From harness data, derive and prove the exact Case-3 formula (tree/branch gadget and cycle-at-distance-k gadget exchange costs, including odd-cycle parity corrections) and confirm impossibility iff graph is a path.

Fix the shortest-cycle-through-S,T computation to be provably exact (address the vertex-disjointness gap in the min-over-edges formula, e.g., via per-edge BFS-layer validation or block-cut decomposition).
Design an O((N+M) log N) or O(N+M) algorithm implementing the verified formula (BFS from S and T, biconnected/block-cut analysis or shortest-cycle-through-two-vertices computation as needed).
Handle edge cases: N=2 single edge, S and T adjacent, path graphs, and validate against the three samples (3, -1, 4).
Write the final Python solution with fast I/O and stress-test it against the brute force on random small graphs before finalizing.
